name: RT-2
summary: RT-2 takes PaLI-X / PaLM-E backbones (5B to 55B) and co-fine-tunes them on internet vision-language data together with RT-1's robot trajectories, writing actions as strings of numbers that occupy otherwise-unused tokens in the text vocabulary. Because the same weights still answer visual questions, semantic knowledge leaks into control: the robot can pick 'the extinct animal' or 'something to use as a hammer' without ever having seen those instructions in robot data.
innovation: Actions-as-text: no new output head, so web pretraining and robot fine-tuning share one objective.
Co-fine-tuning (mixing web data into robot training) rather than sequential fine-tuning, which prevents forgetting semantics.
A chain-of-thought variant that writes a plan in natural language before the action tokens.
matters: Named and defined the VLA category that now dominates manipulation research.
First robot policy that clearly knew things nobody had taught it on a robot.
limits: Fully closed; the 55B model needed cloud inference at 1-3 Hz.
New physical skills did not emerge, only new semantic recombinations of existing motions.
lineage: RT-1's data and action tokenization poured into a web-pretrained VLM backbone.
